title: Parallel Feature Prototyping: How to Run 20 Experiments at Once
summary: A practical guide to spinning up many feature variants in parallel without collisions, data leakage, or merge chaos.
body_text: When product teams want to learn faster, the bottleneck is rarely ideas — it’s isolated execution. Parallel feature prototyping solves that by letting you run multiple variants at the same time, compare them side by side, and ship the winner with confidence. This guide shows how to structure parallel experiments using isolated workspaces, versioned branches, repeatable evaluation, and safe rollout patterns. TL;DR If you want to run 20 experiments at once, the key is to make every experiment self-contained: separate code paths or worktrees per variant isolate data, ports, and services version every prototype compare outcomes with the same evaluation harness ship behind a flag with a kill switch Done right, parallel prototyping turns experimentation from a bottleneck into a system. What Is Parallel Feature Prototyping? Parallel feature prototyping is the practice of building and testing multiple product or code variants simultaneously rather than one after another. Instead of: Build one idea Wait for feedback Throw it away or merge it Start the next idea You: Spin up several isolated variants Evaluate them with the same criteria Compare them side by side Promote the best option This works especially well for teams exploring UI changes, workflow changes, backend behavior, or AI-assisted product experiences. The Core Principle: Zero-Collision Isolation The biggest reason parallel experiments fail is shared state. If two prototypes share the same: port database tables credentials cache keys local files deployment target then they stop being independent experiments. A good parallel prototyping system ensures each variant has its own execution boundary. Common isolation models 1. Git worktrees Use separate worktrees so each experiment gets its own checked-out copy of the repo without constant branch switching. 2. Container-per-feature Run each prototype in a container with its own environment variables, filesystem, and service ports. 3. Branch-based environments Map each prototype to a branch, preview environment, or ephemeral deployment so product and QA can test side by side. For many teams, the best pattern is a combination: git worktree for code isolation, container for runtime isolation, and ephemeral preview for validation. A Practical Architecture for 20 Parallel Experiments A scalable setup usually has five layers: 1. Experiment registry Every prototype gets a name, owner, goal, hypothesis, status, and URL. 2. Isolated workspace Each experiment runs in its own worktree or branch, with explicit paths and dependencies. 3. Runtime sandbox Each variant gets its own container or isolated environment, with unique ports and temporary resources. 4. Shared evaluation harness All variants are tested against the same benchmark, acceptance checks, or user flow. 5. Rollout gate The chosen winner is deployed behind a feature flag with rollback enabled. This structure keeps the experiment loop fast while preserving control. How to Design the Experiment Before You Build It The fastest way to waste time is to prototype without a hypothesis. Use a simple template: Problem: What are we trying to improve? Hypothesis: What do we believe will happen? Variant: What change are we testing? Metric: How will we know it worked? Risk: What could break? Decision rule: What wins, what fails, what needs more data? Example: Problem: users abandon setup during onboarding Hypothesis: reducing the number of steps will increase completion Variant: one-click import flow Metric: onboarding completion rate Risk: lower data quality Decision rule: ship if completion improves without increasing support tickets Side-by-Side Evaluation: Don’t Judge by Vibes If you compare prototypes informally, the loudest opinion wins. Instead, use a repeatable evaluation harness. What to compare task completion time error rate conversion or activation rate developer implementation time support burden maintainability user confusion How to compare same test data same reviewer rubric same performance thresholds same logging and analytics window same launch criteria The goal is to make every variant measurable enough that the outcome is obvious. Failure Modes to Watch For Parallel prototyping introduces its own operational risks. Port collisions If every prototype tries to bind to localhost:3000 , the system breaks immediately. Assign unique ports or use a port allocator. Database leakage A prototype can accidentally read or mutate another experiment’s tables if they share a database. Use separate schemas, separate instances, or disposable test data. Credential leakage The worst-case failure is reusing production credentials across prototypes. Scope secrets per experiment and use short-lived tokens where possible. Network bleed If a variant can reach services it should not touch, it is no longer isolated. Lock down outbound access by default. Branch drift If prototypes run too long, the branch gets stale and merges become painful. Put time limits on experiments and archive dead ends. Versioned Branching and Workflows Branching strategy matters when you are running many prototypes at once. A useful approach is: one base branch for the product line one branch or worktree per experiment one review branch for the winner one mainline branch for approved rollout Keep every prototype versioned so you can reconstruct what changed and why. That makes it easier to: compare variant A against variant B reproduce a winning experiment roll back a bad rollout audit design decisions later Rollout: Ship the Winner Carefully A good experiment does not end when the prototype looks promising. Before rollout: verify the winning variant against your acceptance criteria confirm the metrics moved in the right direction ensure the prototype works in production-like conditions deploy behind a flag keep a kill switch ready A feature flag lets you ship safely without forcing a permanent decision. If the rollout regresses, the kill switch makes rollback immediate. When Parallel Prototyping Is Worth It This approach is ideal when: you have multiple credible ideas the change is expensive enough to justify comparison the team needs faster learning cycles the risk of choosing the wrong option is high you can isolate work cleanly It is less useful when: the task is trivial there is only one viable implementation path the team lacks an evaluation harness experiments cannot be isolated Checklist: Running 20 Experiments Without Chaos Define the hypothesis before building anything Give every experiment a unique name and owner Isolate code with worktrees or branches Isolate runtime with containers or ephemeral environments Assign unique ports, resources, and databases Scope secrets per experiment Use the same evaluation harness for every variant Compare results with the same rubric Track experiment status in a registry Roll out the winner behind a feature flag Keep a kill switch available Conclusion Parallel feature prototyping helps teams move faster without losing control. The trick is not building more experiments — it’s making each one isolated, measurable, and easy to compare. If you can keep code paths separate, lock down runtime boundaries, and evaluate every prototype with the same harness, you can run many experiments at once and still know exactly which one should ship. Want to run feature experiments faster without collisions or rollout risk? Proliferate helps teams structure isolated, parallel workflows so they can prototype, compare, and ship with confidence.

title: Insights into strategic vendor consolidation, part 2: What you should consider first
summary: Learn what to consider before pursuing strategic vendor consolidation in this CGI blog.
body_text: In Insights into strategic vendor consolidation, part 1: Key drivers and benefits, my colleague, Torsten Strass, shares his thoughts on why so many organizations are transitioning from a multi-vendor approach for managed services to strategic vendor consolidation—the selection of one or a few preferred vendors. While using multiple vendors has been the norm in managed services for decades, the complexities and inefficiencies of this approach are making vendor consolidation a more viable and attractive option. In this second blog, I share a few considerations for organizations seeking to pursue vendor consolidation. As Torsten notes, this approach helps organizations achieve “greater alignment, improve operational efficiencies, and drive cost-effectiveness—ultimately maximizing the value of their managed services engagements”—an enticing value proposition for any organization. Consolidating vendors, however, isn’t easy, and some studies show that up to 30% of vendor consolidation initiatives fail. For organizations seeking to reduce their vendor pool, what should they consider before proceeding down this path to ensure the best outcomes? Consideration #1: Business strategy alignment Consolidation requires evaluating your existing vendor pool and selectively narrowing it down to a few reliable and effective partners. How do you determine which vendors to eliminate or keep? Should you add any new vendors? The first consideration to keep in mind is whether a prospective vendor can contribute to the achievement of your overall business strategy for an extended period. What is your defined business strategy? What are the essential requirements for successfully executing it? How does each prospective vendor align with this strategy? Do they have the capabilities to meet your strategic business needs over the long term? Asking these questions helps to identify vendors with a willingness and ability to align with your strategy, embrace your strategic objectives, and commit to delivering the full services required to achieve those objectives. It also helps to identify a true business partner from a transactional service provider. (For more on this topic, I invite you to read my colleague Steve Lippock’s blog, Will the real trusted advisor please stand up? ) Consideration #2: Cost and long-term sustainability Relying on services from multiple vendors makes operations more complex and expensive for CIOs and CTOs. It can lead to an oversized IT vendor portfolio with redundant solutions that negatively impact cost, performance, and risk posture. There also is significant overhead associated with managing multiple negotiations and contracts. Vendor consolidation is a way to simplify operations and save costs. It also helps ensure the delivery of solutions that are sustainable over the long term based on the vendor’s deep knowledge of the client organization. A second consideration, therefore, is whether a prospective vendor’s offerings can advance your financial and long-term sustainability goals. This involves assessing the overall financial cost and impact of the vendor, as well as evaluating whether its solutions will enable you to achieve today’s business objectives while future proofing your business. Consideration #3: Value generation While cost is a key consideration, it’s important to look beyond finances and consider other ways that vendor consolidation can generate business value. Partnership is the essence of vendor consolidation. When vendors become partners aligned with the organization's strategic objectives, the vendor relationship becomes transformative, driving initiatives that transcend traditional vendor-client engagements and deliver more value. This value is achieved through closer alignment and collaboration, enhanced communication, standardized processes, joint innovation, stronger compliance, and more. In pursuing consolidation, consider whether a prospective vendor can generate value for your business in addition to savings costs. This requires a close examination of its capabilities, which, in turn, brings us to the last important consideration. Consideration #4: Vendor capabilities To be successful, vendor consolidation requires careful consideration of a prospective vendor’s ability to deliver required services effectively. What are the vendor’s capabilities and differentiators? Critical areas to examine include the vendor’s managed services experience and track record, industry and technology expertise, range of services, frameworks/processes/tools, governance, innovation practices and outcomes, global and local resources, and alliances. It’s also important to evaluate less tangible qualifications such as the vendor’s partnership approach. Does the vendor collaborate as a partner? Is the vendor committed, trustworthy, accountable, transparent, flexible, and outcome-led? Does it share the same values and align not only with your business strategy but also your culture? One vendor that can deliver holistic capabilities and expected results through a trusted partnership approach is of far more value than multiple vendors that, in practice, operate solely as service providers. Avoiding vendor consolidation failure Vendor consolidation success depends on keeping the above considerations in mind before you embark on a consolidation journey. Ultimately any vendor consolidation exercise needs to enhance the organization’s capabilities, increase efficiencies, drive agility, and infuse new talent. If, based on these considerations, you’re ready to move forward with strategic vendor consolidation, then be sure to read the last blog in this three-part series in which my colleague, Frank van Nistelrooij, shares a multi-phase approach for reducing your vendor pool successfully. As one of the world’s leading managed services partners , CGI is working with clients to explore and implement vendor consolidation strategies and approaches. If you’d like to learn more about our work and the outcomes that we’re helping clients to achieve, feel free to contact me .

title: Exploring Connected Wearable Data, Part 1: Oura
body_text: In this article First, a quick explanation of our data exploration methodology and a few definitions The cholesterol-sleep relationship in women over the age of 40 How does this differ for men? So, why are cholesterol and sleep related? Supplementary Data Are you finding it difficult to achieve restful sleep or feeling drained despite using your sleep tracker? Discover how combining sleep data from devices like Oura rings or Apple Watches with blood biomarker data can transform your health and well-being. Many of us rely on wearable devices to monitor our sleep, hoping to uncover the secrets to better rest and more energy. However, these devices often leave us with more questions than answers. It’s not just about tracking steps or sleep stages; it’s about understanding the deeper connections between different aspects of our health. If you’re looking to improve your diet, exercise, or sleep habits, the following insights can help you determine what changes might enhance your overall well-being. [1] To explore these connections, we analyzed SiPhox user data to identify relationships between blood biomarker data and connected wearable device data. S urprisingly, we discovered a strong correlation between lipids and sleep data, particularly in women over the age of 40. These findings could provide valuable insights for those looking to make informed changes to their health routines. [2] First, a quick explanation of our data exploration methodology and a few definitions Methodology Wearable data was averaged over the two weeks preceding the associated blood tests. For correlation analysis, we used Pearson’s correlation coefficient (a measure of the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables) to measure the strength and direction of the linear relationship between the two datasets. We further visualized these relationships by creating plots with an Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression line (a straight line that best fits the data points), which helped illustrate the trend and strength of the correlations. This methodology allowed us to effectively identify and visualize meaningful correlations within the data. [3] [4] Cholesterol — the Good, the Bad, and the Transport: Cholesterol can be categorized into HDL-C (high-density lipoprotein cholesterol) and LDL-C (low-density lipoprotein cholesterol), commonly referred to as “good” and “bad” cholesterol. LDL-C (“bad”) cholesterol is deposited into the arteries, which increases the risk of cardiovascular disease. [5] HDL-C refers to the cholesterol carried by Apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1) (a type of protein that carries cholesterol in the blood) -containing HDL particles. HDL particles pick up harmful cholesterol in the arteries and then carry everything to the liver (directly or indirectly), where cholesterol is repurposed or removed. [6] [7] Rapid Eye Movement Sleep : Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep is a phase that lasts approx. 25% of your total sleep duration, where (alongside other activities) your brain rests and repairs itself so you can wake up feeling refreshed and energized. [8] The cholesterol-sleep relationship in women over the age of 40 There was a strong positive correlation between HDL-C and REM sleep for women over 40 years of age. Interestingly, there was no significant correlation between the same markers in neither men of the same age group ( correlation coefficient = 0.08 ) nor in younger women ( correlation coefficient = -0.13 ). Unsurprisingly, we saw a similarly positive correlation between APOA1 and REM sleep, which is to be expected given the relationship between HDL-C (passenger) and APOA1 (vehicle). For additional graphs on the relationship between bad cholesterol (LDL-C, APOB) and sleep data in the same age group, please refer to the Supplementary Data section. How does this differ for men? Given the strong correlation in women, one might assume that there’d be a similar correlation in men. But our data says otherwise. The correlation between HDL-C and REM, for men over 40, was only 0.08, which is essentially a non-existent correlation and certainly a far weaker one than the 0.53 correlation coefficient in women of the same age group! For all intents and purposes, our data indicates that there is no correlation between cholesterol biomarkers and sleep data in men over 40. So, why are cholesterol and sleep related? It is unclear whether the relationship we’re observing is causative or correlative. Perhaps one of the two, HDL-C or REM sleep, impacts the other. Just as likely, they’re both independently impacted by another set of biomarkers or activities, such as an active lifestyle or hormone status. That being said, here are a few mechanistic connections between REM and HDL-C: HDL-C particles have significant anti-inflammatory properties . Chronic inflammation is known to disrupt sleep patterns. So this reduced inflammation could contribute to more stable and prolonged REM sleep. HDL-C particles support endothelial function, which is vital for healthy blood circulation. Improved endothelial function could improve circulation to the brain during sleep, and subsequent REM sleep duration. [9] These connections exist in both men and women, though. If either or both of these are the root cause of the correlation, then why don’t we see this in men? Or a younger cohort of women? If you’re interested in seeing how your cholesterol and sleep are correlated, pick up an at-home blood testing kit from SiPhox . You’ll receive results and insights in your SiPhox dashboard within a few days of collecting your sample. Supplementary Data Correlation between HDL-C and REM sleep among males aged 40 and older. Correlation between LDL-C and REM sleep among females aged 40 and older. Correlation between hbA1C and Oura sleep score among females aged 47 and older. Correlation between HDL-C and REM sleep among females aged 20 to 40 years. Correlation between APOB and REM sleep among females aged 40 and older. title: Best Accounting Reconciliation Software for July 2026: Top Tools Compared
summary: Compare the best accounting reconciliation software for July 2026. QuickBooks, Xero, Trintech, BlackLine, and Double reviewed for small business to enterprise
body_text: Picking automated reconciliation software means choosing between tools that match transactions and tools that manage your entire close process. Some stop at bank feeds, others handle intercompany eliminations and accrual schedules. Free tiers exist, but meaningful automation sits behind a paywall, and the price gap between small business tools and enterprise platforms is wider than you'd expect. We compared what you actually get at each level so you know where to start based on your volume, compliance needs, and how much of the process you want to automate. TLDR: Automated reconciliation software cuts reconciliation time by 85% compared to manual methods You need different tools based on volume: QuickBooks or Xero for small teams, Trintech or BlackLine for enterprise Free tools work for personal accounts, but paid versions offer audit trails and multi-source integrations AI-powered tools learn from your matching patterns and read unstructured data like PDF statements Double connects your reconciliation work to month-end close tracking with preparer and reviewer workflows What Is Accounting Reconciliation Software Accounting reconciliation software is a category of financial tech that compares records across two or more sources to confirm they match. Think bank statements against your general ledger , or accounts payable against vendor invoices. When the numbers align, your books are clean. When they don't, the software flags the gap so you can investigate. Before dedicated tools existed, this work lived in spreadsheets. You'd export data, paste it side by side, and manually hunt for discrepancies. Automated reconciliation software replaces that process by pulling records directly from your accounting system or bank feed, running comparisons on your behalf, and surfacing only the items that need attention. Key Benefits of Automated Reconciliation Software The benefits of automated reconciliation show up where they matter: time, accuracy, and cost. Deloitte's Finance Trends 2026 research found that 63% of finance leaders are actively using AI. The results track: companies implementing AI-powered reconciliation solutions report 85% faster reconciliations compared to manual methods. For a team processing dozens of accounts each month, that's a real difference in how the close gets done. Accuracy improves too. Manual matching is vulnerable to copy-paste errors and formula mistakes that quietly compound. Automated tools apply consistent logic on every run, no exceptions. Fewer errors on the first pass means less rework downstream, and a close cycle that doesn't drag into the following week. Types of Reconciliations Accounting Software Can Handle Not every reconciliation workflow is the same, and the right software depends on which types you actually need to run. Bank reconciliation matches bank statements to the general ledger. Credit card reconciliation compares card statements to expense records in your accounting system. Balance sheet reconciliation confirms every balance sheet account ties to documented support. Intercompany reconciliation eliminates cross-entity transactions before consolidated reporting. Accrual reconciliation handles prepaid expenses, accrued liabilities, and deferred revenue against recognition schedules. Some tools handle all five. Others focus on bank feeds and stop there. Knowing your mix before you shop saves time and keeps you from paying for features you will never use. Core Features to Consider in Reconciliation Tools Reconciliation tools aren't all built the same, and the features that matter most depend heavily on your volume, team size, and how complex your financial data is. Here are the core capabilities worth reviewing before committing to any tool: Automated matching lets the software pair transactions across sources without manual input, which cuts down on hours spent cross-referencing spreadsheets. Multi-source data ingestion means the tool can pull from bank feeds, ERPs, payment processors, and spreadsheets simultaneously. Audit trails give you a timestamped log of every change, which matters for compliance and internal reviews. Exception management surfaces unresolved or flagged items so your team can focus on what needs attention. Reporting and export options determine how usable your reconciliation data is downstream. Free vs. Paid Capabilities Many tools advertise free tiers, but the meaningful automation usually sits behind a paywall. Free tools like bank reconciliation in Excel or basic checkbook software cover simple personal use cases well. If you're running a business with hundreds of monthly transactions, the limitations of free tools become apparent quickly. Paid tools like Trintech Cadency or AssureNet offer certification workflows, match configuration, and role-based access that free options don't touch. Bank Reconciliation Software for Small Business vs. Enterprise Small businesses and enterprise finance teams have very different needs from reconciliation software, and the right fit depends on transaction volume, team size, and how much automation you actually need. For small businesses, the priorities are usually affordability, ease of setup, and basic bank feed syncing. For enterprise teams, the focus moves to multi-entity support, audit trails, role-based access, and integrations with ERP systems. Here is a quick breakdown of what to look for at each level: Small business owners often start with free or low-cost options like Wave or a free checkbook register. Enterprise teams typically invest in dedicated tools like Trintech or BlackLine , where the depth of audit logging and workflow controls support the higher cost. The gap between the two is wide, but knowing which side you sit on makes the rest of your decision much easier. Choosing the Right Reconciliation Software for Your Organization The right fit depends on your organization's size, complexity, and how much of the process you want to automate. Small businesses often do well with tools like QuickBooks or Xero, which fold bank reconciliation into broader accounting workflows. Larger teams with high transaction volumes tend to need dedicated solutions like Trintech Cadency or ReconNet. Software Best For Key Strengths Starting Price Range Double Teams managing month-end close with reconciliation needs Connects reconciliation to close workflows with preparer and reviewer sign-offs, real-time tracking, and balance sheet account ownership Contact for enterprise pricing QuickBooks Small businesses with straightforward accounting needs Bank feed syncing built into full accounting software, easy setup, widely adopted by small business accountants $30-90/month Xero Small to mid-size businesses needing multi-currency support Bank reconciliation integrated with invoicing and payroll, strong third-party app marketplace, cloud-native design $13-70/month Wave Freelancers and very small businesses with minimal volume Free core accounting and bank reconciliation, simple interface, good for personal checkbook tracking Free for basic features Trintech Cadency Enterprise teams with SOX compliance requirements Configurable matching rules (one-to-one, many-to-many), certification workflows, full audit trails with timestamps and user attribution Contact for enterprise pricing BlackLine Large organizations needing multi-entity consolidation Automated intercompany eliminations, balance sheet substantiation, integrates with major ERP systems like SAP and Oracle Contact for enterprise pricing ReconNet Mid-market to enterprise teams processing high transaction volumes Dedicated reconciliation focus with exception management, supports multiple data sources, role-based access controls Contact for pricing A few questions worth asking before you decide: How many accounts and entities require reconciliation each month? Do you need audit trails and compliance reporting, or just basic matching? Is a free or low-cost tool sufficient, or does your volume support a paid solution? Common Implementation Challenges and How to Tackle Them Switching to a new reconciliation tool rarely goes smoothly on day one. Here are the friction points teams run into most often, and what actually helps. Data migration headaches are common when historical transaction records exist in incompatible formats. Running a parallel close during the first month gives your team a safety net while the new system proves itself. User adoption slows when staff are used to manual spreadsheet workflows. Short, role-specific training sessions work better than long all-hands demos. Integration gaps with existing ERP or payroll systems can delay go-live timelines. Confirming API availability before purchasing saves considerable rework later. Audit trail requirements vary by industry. Make sure the tool you choose logs every change with timestamps and user attribution before committing to a contract. How Reconciliation Software Supports Audit and Compliance Requirements Auditors want more than a final number. They want to see how you got there. Reconciliation software builds that trail as you work: every match, exception, and sign-off gets logged with timestamps and user attribution, so audit requests don't turn into a week of digging through old files. For teams covered by SOX, preparer and reviewer sign-off workflows are non-negotiable. Software that enforces those approval chains creates documented evidence of control compliance that holds up under scrutiny. GAAP consistency follows the same logic. When reconciliation rules run identically each period, the system captures that consistency for you instead of relying on institutional memory to prove it later. The Role of AI in Accounting Reconciliation Software Basic automation applies fixed matching rules. AI learns from them and adjusts. Rossum's research found that 49% of finance departments still rely entirely on manual data entry and spreadsheets, with zero automation in place. Half the market hasn't automated at all, which makes the AI conversation feel premature for many teams. But for those that have crossed that threshold, the capability gap between rule-based tools and AI-powered ones is real. 49% of finance departments still rely entirely on manual processes, with no automation in place. Half the market hasn't automated at all, which makes the AI conversation feel premature for many teams. But for those that have crossed that threshold, the capability gap between rule-based tools and AI-powered ones is real. AI-powered reconciliation tools adapt over time instead of running the same static logic each period. They learn from historical matching patterns, surface transactions that deviate from prior behavior, and can read unstructured data like PDF statements or free-text bank descriptions to extract transaction details automatically. Free vs. Paid Reconciliation Software: What You Get at Each Level The right tier depends on your situation. Free tools work well for individuals tracking personal accounts or small businesses with simple needs, but they come with real limits around volume, automation, and support. Here is a quick breakdown of what to expect at each level: Feature Free Tier Paid Tier Transaction volume Low (often capped) High or unlimited Automation Basic or none Rule-based and AI-driven Integrations Limited Banks, ERPs, and more Audit trail Minimal Full history and reporting Support Community only Dedicated support Free tools like Wave or a basic Excel template cover personal checkbook tracking and simple bank reconciliation. Paid tools handle the heavier work: multi-entity reconciliation, automated matching, and compliance reporting . Month-End Close Management with Double Double is a smart month-end close solution built for accounting teams that need more than a spreadsheet can offer. It brings together task management, workflows, and real-time close tracking in one place, so nothing falls through the cracks at the end of the month. Where reconciliation software stops at matching transactions, the broader close process . Every balance sheet account gets owned, reviewed, and signed off on time. Final Thoughts on Finding Your Reconciliation Solution Reconciliation software works best when it matches the close you're actually running. Automated reconciliation tools save time by handling the repetitive matching work, but only if they connect to the systems you already use. Start with your transaction count and compliance needs, then find the fit that makes sense for your team.

title: Which HDB Town Has the Most Million-Dollar Flats? (2026 Data)
summary: Toa Payoh tops Singapore's HDB million-dollar flat rankings. See the full list and 4 towns that haven't had a single one.
body_text: Last Updated on July 17, 2026 by Yolly Del Prado TL;DR / Summary: – Toa Payoh has sold 748 million-dollar HDB flats as of July 2026, the most of any town in Singapore. – 929 flats have crossed $1 million in 2026 alone, bringing the all-time total to 4,953. – Chua Chu Kang, Jurong West, Sembawang, and Tengah have never had a single million-dollar sale. You’ve probably seen the headlines. Some HDB flat somewhere sold for over a million dollars, again . What most of those headlines skip is that it’s basically always the same handful of towns doing this. Toa Payoh has the most , by a wide margin: 748 flats have sold for at least $1 million as of July 2026 . The next town on the list isn’t even close, less than half that number. And this isn’t some rare, once-in-a-while thing anymore. 929 HDB resale flats have crossed the million-dollar mark in 2026 so far . Go back to the very first one in 2012 and add them all up, and you get 4,953 total. Sounds like it’s everywhere, right? It’s not. Some towns are packed with these sales. Others have had exactly zero. So which camp is your town in? Let’s find out. Disclaimer: Figures and rankings in this article are accurate as of time of publication (July 2026) and are based on available resale transaction data. Property prices and market standings may change over time. The Full Ranking: Top 10 Towns with the Most Million-Dollar HDB Flats (as of July 2026) Here’s how the towns stack up based on the number of million-dollar HDB flats sold: Rank Town Transactions Average Price Highest Sale 1 Toa Payoh 748 $1,137,142 $1,600,000 2 Bukit Merah 630 $1,127,166 $1,728,000 (all-time HDB record) 3 Queenstown 573 $1,135,006 $1,700,000 4 Kallang/Whampoa 505 $1,118,149 $1,568,000 5 Bishan 410 $1,158,165 $1,632,000 6 Central Area 398 $1,213,392 $1,630,000 7 Ang Mo Kio 295 $1,109,367 $1,500,000 8 Clementi 280 $1,150,947 $1,580,000 9 Geylang 160 $1,067,386 $1,375,000 10 Tampines 144 $1,059,690 $1,240,000 The towns at the top all have something in common, and it’s not just luck. Why These Towns Keep Showing Up It comes down to a familiar mix. These are mostly mature estates, which means they’ve had decades to build up demand, strong MRT connections, and a reputation that buyers are willing to pay for. And it’s not only about the town itself. Many of the flats crossing $1 million are also larger units, sitting on higher floors, with longer remaining leases than what you’d find in an older block down the road. Put those together in a town with limited resale supply, and prices climb fast. It’s not really a mystery why Toa Payoh and Bukit Merah keep topping these lists. They check almost every box a buyer is chasing, all at once. The Towns With Zero Million-Dollar Flats Now for the flip side. Four HDB towns have never had a single flat cross the million-dollar mark, as of July 2026: Chua Chu Kang , Jurong West , Sembawang , and Tengah . That doesn’t mean flats there are cheap. It just means these towns are still catching up. They’re newer, further from the city centre, and most of their flats haven’t hit the point where big units, high floors, and long leases start piling up in one place. Give it a few years. As more flats here clear their Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) with leases still comfortably above 90 years, it’s only a matter of time before one of these towns shows up on this list. Ranking High (or Low) Doesn’t Decide Your Flat’s Price Living in a town near the top of this list doesn’t automatically mean your flat is worth seven figures, and living in one at the bottom doesn’t mean it isn’t worth a good price either. A million-dollar sale still comes down to the specific unit. Floor level, remaining lease, flat size, and how close you are to an MRT station all matter more than which town you’re in. If you’re trying to figure out what your own flat could actually fetch, a town-wide average won’t tell you much. You’d get a far more accurate picture from an actual valuation of your unit, whether that’s through a property agent who knows the area or Ohmyhome’s evaluation tool HomerAI. https://ohmyhome.com/en-sg/homer-evaluation?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=clickthru&utm_campaign=HDBTownWithMostMilliionDollarHDB Looking to Buy or Sell a Property? Rankings like this are fun to scroll through, and yeah, maybe a little validating if your town made the cut. But at some point you’re going to want to know about your own flat specifically, not just the town it’s in. If you’re planning to sell your HDB unit , our in-house Super Agents at Ohmyhome can guide you through the whole process and help you land the best possible price, no matter where your town sits on this list. On the other hand, if you’re planning to buy a new home, we’ll help you find something that actually fits your budget and preferences. Simply submit your details and we’ll match you with your ideal home. Have questions or need assistance? WhatsApp us today. Frequently Asked Questions Why do some smaller HDB flats sell for more than bigger flat types? Smaller flats can outsell bigger ones when they sit in premium locations that rarely turn over on the resale market. A handful of 3-room flats have crossed $1 million with average prices higher than 5-room units, simply because so few of them exist in sought-after estates. Scarcity ends up mattering more than square footage. If I’m buying for long-term value, should I target a top-ranked town like Toa Payoh? Not necessarily, since a high ranking reflects past sales, not guaranteed future growth. Towns like Toa Payoh may already be near their ceiling for certain unit types, while a newer town with rising MRT connectivity could have more room to grow. Ranking tells you where the demand has been, not where it’s headed next. How much does floor level actually affect a flat’s price in these transactions? Floor level plays a bigger role than most buyers expect, sometimes adding well over $100,000 to an otherwise similar unit. Higher floors usually come with better views, less noise, and more privacy, which buyers are willing to pay a premium for. Two flats with identical size and lease can still land in very different price brackets. Which town is likely to be the next to join this million-dollar list? Towns with rising MRT connectivity and flats nearing key lease milestones are the most likely next entrants, though no single town is guaranteed. Places like Yishun or Woodlands, both already inching close with recent high sales, are worth watching.

title: Will the Fed have to raise rates this year?
summary: Rising goods inflation, tariffs and deglobalization may complicate the Fed’s efforts to reach its 2% inflation target, limiting the likelihood of rate cuts.
body_text: Will the Fed have to raise rates this year? Rising goods prices, tariff pressures and the long-term effects of deglobalization are creating new obstacles on the path back to the Fed’s inflation target 5 min read KEY POINTS Core goods inflation has turned positive again, reversing a long-standing trend that once helped keep overall inflation in check. Tariffs, supply chain shifts and deglobalization are adding inflationary pressures that could make it harder for the Fed to achieve its 2% target. With inflation risks persisting, the Federal Reserve may be forced to maintain a tighter monetary policy stance for longer than markets expect. While the oil markets are playing a role in the now-increasing odds of a rate move at the July Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, there are additional reasons to be cautious as we think about inflation returning to the Fed’s 2% target. It is also important to keep in mind that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has clearly stated that this target is the top priority for monetary policy. Shelter, the largest weighting in the Fed’s “core” inflation measures, has been moderating as home prices nationally have slowed their ascent and some markets are seeing outright declines. However, core services, a segment where wages are the biggest cost component, have been moving higher and, as our chart this week shows, core goods inflation is moving higher as well. In this week’s chart, we show tariffs as one explanatory factor for the rise in goods inflation but there are other factors at work too. Pre-pandemic core goods were a consistent dis-inflationary part of the overall inflation picture. In fact, one of the key benefits of the globalization of the economy was the ability for companies to seek lower-cost production which led to steadily decreasing goods pricing. As the pandemic interrupted the flow of goods, supply chains became disrupted and the rate of inflation on core goods skyrocketed. Even as time allowed the flow of goods to improve, companies began making different decisions on where to locate production and to find ways to lessen the risk of similar events in the future. Even with this shift is production caused by the pandemic, core goods returned to a dis-inflationary part of the picture until tariff policies came into focus. Since then, core goods inflation has turned positive and now exceeds the Fed’s 2% target on its own. This can complicate the decision-making process for the FOMC going forward as a segment which had been additive to achieving an overall 2% inflation rate is now a headwind. To be sure, tariff policies have come under scrutiny, and some policies have been reversed by the Supreme Court, but the president recently announced additional tariffs which could reinforce some of the underlying trends in place. Warsh and the rest of the FOMC have a difficult job. Forecasting what might happen geopolitically is nigh impossible, yet the implications this all could have on price levels and the ability to see inflation move back towards the 2% target are real. Our overall sense is that getting back to 2% in an environment of deglobalization, enhanced geopolitical stress, abundant liquidity and growing negativity around the U.S.’s fiscal position will make rate cuts very difficult. We don’t think the Fed needs to aggressively raise rates, but the bias toward monetary policy from here has shifted towards tightening.
